paraphrase: Ānanda reports that Pūraṇa Kassapa describes six classes of birth: black (butchers, hunters, bandits, executioners and those of cruel livelihood), blue (mendicants who live 'by thorns' and others who teach deeds and action), red (Nigaṇṭhas with one cloth), yellow (white-clothed lay disciples of the naked ones), white (Ājīvaka men and women), and supremely white (Nanda Vaccha, Kisa Saṅkicca and Makkhali Gosāla). The Buddha says Pūraṇa laid this down without the consent of the world, like forcing a piece of meat on a poor man and demanding payment.
notes: Reported by an opponent: Ānanda and the Buddha (AN 6.57, Buddhist Pali canon). Section refs = SuttaCentral (bilara) segmentation, checked in the local e-text. DN 2 ascribes the six classes to Makkhali; AN 6.57 to Pūraṇa — both recorded as the texts give them.

paraphrase: The Buddha's own six classes: born in a dark (low) state one may produce a dark result, a bright result, or nibbāna that is neither dark nor bright; born in a bright (high) state one may likewise produce a dark result, a bright result, or nibbāna — the last by going forth, abandoning the five hindrances, establishing mindfulness and developing the awakening factors.
speaker: the Buddha

differs_from.note: reinterprets the six classes by conduct, not by sect or fate
